assessment_summary: The statement claims that any tournament on exactly 4 vertices contains a Hamiltonian cycle. This is false because a tournament contains a Hamiltonian cycle if and only if it is strongly connected. A transitive tournament on 4 vertices is a valid tournament but is not strongly connected (it contains no directed cycles at all). Therefore, the statement is false and any proof attempt is impossible.
counterexample: A transitive tournament on 4 vertices (e.g. vertices A, B, C, D with edges A->B, A->C, A->D, B->C, B->D, C->D) contains no directed cycles, and thus no Hamiltonian cycle.
